answer: An agent marketplace requires each seller, whether offering code or quill drawings, to lock a $100 bond for a 30-day horizon before accepting work. A verifiable failure to deliver forfeits the bond. Creating hollow identities therefore cannot produce free selling capacity: running 1,000 eligible accounts ties up $100,000, and abandoning accounts after proven fraud burns their bonds. The defense makes scale costly without pretending each account is a unique person.
